components.description: Limits of existing designs motivate an FSM-based, auto-designed multi-agent framework evaluated on text, ML and coding tasks

nodes.name: Manual multi-agent design is costly
nodes.description: Most existing multi-agent systems are manually designed, requiring human effort for complex codebases and iterations of polishing, and target only specific scenarios.

nodes.name: Existing auto-design methods are limited
nodes.description: SPP, AutoAgents and EvoAgent design a system per specific case and lack generalization; SPP and AutoAgents lack tool use; ADAS and Symbolic-Learning need many iterations and external data.

nodes.name: Existing communication structures lack traceback
nodes.description: Linear, decentralized-debate and orchestrator structures have limited ability to trace back to fix errors or misunderstandings from previous steps.

nodes.name: Other structures are constrained FSMs
nodes.description: A linear structure is an FSM with one transition per state and no traceback or verifier; decentralized debate has limited traceback to the first state; an orchestrator system is an FSM with a shared condition verifier.

nodes.name: FSM suits auto-design
nodes.description: An FSM with a customized condition verifier per state and unconstrained transition conditions maximizes flexibility and is well suited to automatic design.

nodes.name: MetaAgent design procedure
nodes.description: Given a task-type description, MetaAgent designs the needed agents, summarizes states for the possible situations, and gives each state a task-solving agent, instructions, a condition verifier and listener agents.

nodes.name: FSM deployment loop with traceback
nodes.description: At deployment the task-solving agent's output is checked by the condition verifier against transition conditions; if one matches the system moves to the next state, which can be an earlier state to allow traceback, and the output is saved as memory.

nodes.name: Initial FSM chains are too long
nodes.description: The initial FSM design often has excessively long chains of information transfer and task solving that hinder performance.

nodes.name: State-merging optimization
nodes.description: MetaAgent traverses each pair of states and uses an LLM to decide mergeability, eliminating trivial states, without needing external data or many iterations.

nodes.name: Text-based task results
nodes.description: MetaAgent scores 0.86 on Trivial Creative Writing and 0.60 on GPQA (Diamond), above Direct, CoT, CoT-SC, llm-debate, Self-Refine and SPP (0.79 and 0.45), surpassing prior prompt-based SOTA by 9%.

nodes.name: ML Bench results
nodes.description: On ML Bench, MetaAgent beats all auto-designed frameworks, is SOTA on Titanic and House Prices, second-best elsewhere, and reaches 97% of the best human-designed system's average performance.

nodes.name: Software development results
nodes.description: On software development tasks MetaAgent passes 50% more checkpoints than the human-designed MetaGPT and outperforms other auto-designed frameworks.

nodes.name: Tool use ablation
nodes.description: Disabling tool use lowers performance on Trivial Creative Writing and GPQA (Diamond), showing the search engine helps.

nodes.name: Traceback ablation
nodes.description: Systems without traceback often fail due to unresolved bugs, e.g. a tester cannot relay a bug back to the programmer.

nodes.name: Optimization ablation
nodes.description: Removing the optimization causes a sharp performance drop, with failures from excessively long text in bad cases.

nodes.name: Lower deployment token cost
nodes.description: MetaAgent achieves higher or comparable performance at relatively lower token cost than other methods, and its task-level design is cheaper and more broadly applicable than case-level design such as AutoAgents.

isolated_nodes.name: Designer and executor model quality
isolated_nodes.description: On ML Bench, GPT-4o as both designer and executor scores 0.83, while replacing the designer or executor with GPT-3.5-Turbo drops it to 0.26 and 0.35, with executor quality mattering more.

structural_reasoning: Limitations of prior designs motivate the FSM framework; its design and optimization feed into the empirical results and ablations.
